messages:
alexa: FYI: noticed a small but consistent perf regression after yesterday's driver rollout. p99 up ~3% for requests with seqlen>512. Traces point to extra KV lookups + fallbacks.
cheng: can you share the persisted key format?
alexa: current persisted key: `model:{model_hash}:kv:{shard}` — seems we never included driver id or config. fallback path kicks in when driver toggles kernel path and we miss a compatible key.
sarah: ouch. that explains the misses. adding driver id makes sense. also need model version.
omar: adding fields will increase key cardinality. we should be careful about explosion + storage. what's the hit rate delta?
alexa: from profiling: KV hit rate for bin>512 dropped from 98.5% -> 92.1% post-rollout. avg lookup latency for those requests went 0.45ms -> 1.7ms. CPU wait on main thread increased ~0.8ms per request when we hit fallback.
riya: timeline? is this only for the new kernel path?
alexa: yes, mostly when kernel selector switches to v2 kernels for arch=a100 and seqlen bin>=512. older kernels still use the old namespace so cross-driver compatibility broke.
cheng: proposed key: ``model:{model_hash}:ver:{model_version}:driver:{driver_id}:cfg:{cfg_hash}:bin:{seqlen_bin}:shard:{shard}``
sarah: +1 but also mark whether key is persistent or ephemeral. e.g. append `:ttl_scope=ephemeral` or `:persist=1`. helps GC.
omar: alternatives: 1) keep compact key but add `driver_compat` map elsewhere, 2) derive driver-agnostic compatibility tags on write. both avoid full combinatorial keys.
riya: we need clear invalidation semantics on driver/runtime/model changes. right now model reloads don't bump keys so stale entries remain. recommend adding `model_epoch` monotonic counter included in key on writes.
alexa: agree. plan: include `model_epoch` + `driver_id`. this allows old driver keys to be skipped and swept. suggestion for persistence: dual-write during rollout window (write both old and new key) then sweep old after 24h.
cheng: can we do lazy backfill instead? on first miss, write new key from old value and continue. cheaper upfront but spikes on first traffic.
sarah: lazy backfill seems safest for storage. combine with background compaction job to migrate hot keys. compaction job should respect throttle.
omar: will write GC/compaction design: prefix-scan old keys -> move to new key -> mark tombstone on old -> eventual delete. need rate limits and circuit breaker.
deploy-bot: deployment notice: driver-chooser v2 was rolled 2026-03-02T12:03Z. canary fraction 10% -> 100% yesterday.iya: rollout timing probably caused most customer traffic to experience mismatch.
alexa: action items: 1) alexa prototype new key + dual-write shim (ETA 2d). 2) cheng run perf bench with synthetic seqlen distribution and report hit rate + latency (ETA 1d). 3) sarah update cache runbook & TTL guidelines (ETA 3d). 4) omar design compaction/gc job and rate limits (ETA 4d). 5) riya coordinate canary rollback plan if regressions worsen.
cheng: quick ask — can you paste the exact bin boundaries you used for seqlen? need them for bench.
alexa: bins: [0-64,65-256,257-512,513-1024,1025+]. v2 kernel only used for 513+.
sarah: want a short rollforward checklist: dual-write flag, metrics monitor (kv_hit_rate, kv_miss_latency, p99), canary rollback toggle, compaction window. i'll add to runbook.
omar: note: also ensure the persistence store supports atomic rename for backfill to avoid dupes. if not, add idempotent move.
riya: will schedule a 30m sync tomorrow morning to sign off.
alexa: thanks all — ping me in thread if you see anything odd. :thumbsup:
sarah: ack :white_check_mark:
cheng: will post micro-bench results in this thread.
riya: adding alert: `kv.namespace.misses > 1%` for >5m to our paging rules (tentative).
alexa: perfect — appreciate the quick triage.
